dedupe_keys.name: osmnxr r toolkit to download model and analyse openstreetmap street networks osmnx inspired rust core

description: osmnxr is an R package, inspired by the Python library OSMnx, for downloading, modelling, simplifying, analysing and visualising street networks and other features from OpenStreetMap. The CRAN page read on 2026-09-28 (version 0.1.1, published 5 July 2026, DOI 10.32614/CRAN.package.osmnxr) says it builds routable graphs from a place name, address, point or bounding box, simplifies their topology, computes shortest paths, isochrones and urban metrics such as intersection density, circuity, street orientation entropy and centrality, and exports to the sf, sfnetworks and MapLibre formats, with heavy graph computation done by a bundled Rust core; vignettes cover accessibility, points of interest, routing and street orientation. Coverage is anywhere OpenStreetMap maps streets. Access is free under the MIT licence. Caveats: it is a first release that needs a Rust toolchain to build, and results inherit OpenStreetMap gaps. It supports network flow and exposure studies in R, such as measuring which neighbourhoods lose access to hospitals when flooded road links are removed. Related record: OSMnx, the Python library it follows.
inputs: OpenStreetMap data by place name, address, point or bounding box
name: osmnxr: R toolkit to download, model and analyse OpenStreetMap street networks (OSMnx-inspired, Rust core)
outputs: urban network metrics (intersection density, circuity, orientation entropy, centrality)
